VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Newcore Gold Ltd. ("Newcore" or the "Company") (TSX-V: NCAU, OTCQX: NCAUF) is pleased to announce the submission of a Mining Lease application for the Company's Enchi Gold Project ("Enchi" or the "Project") in Ghana. The Mining Lease application covers 53.37 km2 of the 248 km2 property.

Honourable Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, Minister for Lands & Natural Resources, Ghana stated, "The Government of Ghana welcomes Newcore's submission of a Mining Lease application for the Enchi Gold Project. The Project is one of the most advanced large-scale gold projects in development in Ghana and has the potential to create long-term benefits through job creation, local community support and contribution to national revenues. We support investment that develops our resources responsibly and creates long-term value for Ghanaians, while meeting the highest environmental standards. The Ministry looks forward to working closely with Newcore and the Minerals Commission as the application moves through the review process, with the goal of granting a Mining Lease for the Enchi Gold Project in the first half of 2027."

Luke Alexander, President, CEO and Director of Newcore stated, "The submission of the Mining Lease application is a key step in the permitting process for our Enchi Gold Project in Ghana. It represents the first stage in the permitting path, de-risking and advancing the Project to development-ready status. The Government of Ghana has shown strong support for Enchi, and we look forward to continuing to work with the government, local communities and all stakeholders as we advance the Enchi Gold Project's development path to production."

The Company anticipates that the review process for the Mining Lease application will be completed by mid-2027. Once the mining lease is granted, the Company can formally start its application to the Ghana Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) for an environmental permit. This next step will be supported by environmental monitoring and baseline work that has been on-going at Enchi since 2015, along with environmental and social baseline studies completed for the Project in 2015, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026. The studies completed have concluded that there are no existing issues related to water, soil, noise or air quality for the proposed development of the Project. The most recent studies were completed by Abbakus Geosocial Consult Limited based in Accra, Ghana, an independent group with extensive experience focused on mining projects in Ghana. The Project is looked upon favourably by the local communities and stakeholders and is in an area with a long history of gold exploration, development, and mining.

About Newcore Gold Ltd.
Newcore Gold is advancing its Enchi Gold Project located in Ghana, Africa's largest gold producer (1). Newcore Gold offers investors a unique combination of top-tier leadership, who are aligned with shareholders through their 12% equity ownership, and prime district scale exploration opportunities. Enchi's 248 km2 land package covers 40 kilometres of Ghana's prolific Bibiani Shear Zone, a gold belt which hosts several multi-million-ounce gold deposits, including the Chirano mine 50 kilometres to the north. Newcore's vision is to build a responsive, creative and powerful gold enterprise that maximizes returns for shareholders.

Reflects Strengthening Financial Profile, Strong Cash Flow Generation, Successful Balance Sheet De-Leveraging Below 3x, and Confidence in Continued Momentum

INDIANAPOLIS, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Elanco Animal Health Incorporated (NYSE: ELAN) announced today its Board of Directors has authorized the repurchase of up to $600 million of the company's common stock. The authorization reflects Elanco's accelerating operational momentum, robust free cash flow generation, strengthened balance sheet and clear path to net leverage ratio of 2.0 to 2.5 times.

After reaching the targeted sub 3.0x net leverage ratio, the company is updating its capital allocation priorities. Elanco will remain focused on a combination of debt paydown and accretive growth opportunities including continued investment in innovation, while starting a multi-year share repurchase program to drive enhanced, long-term shareholder value.

"Today's authorization of our first-ever share repurchase program reflects Elanco's financial transformation into a consistent, reliable growth company with more than three years of steady quarterly growth," said Jeff Simmons, President and CEO of Elanco. "Our disciplined execution against our Innovation, Portfolio and Productivity (IPP) strategy and expectations of a multi-year runway of mid-single digit revenue growth, high single digit adjusted EBITDA growth and low double digit adjusted EPS growth give us the financial flexibility to accelerate capital return to shareholders, while continuing to fully fund our growth priorities and pipeline to ensure a consistent flow of high-impact innovation."

Over the past several years, Elanco has prioritized debt reduction, successfully reducing its net leverage ratio (NLR) by approximately three-quarters of a turn in 2026 year-to-date alone. Earlier this month, the company reported a major strategic milestone as NLR fell below 3.0x faster than anticipated, unlocking accelerated capital allocation flexibility.

"Our continued strong operational performance and momentum achieving sub-3.0x leverage ahead of schedule gives us confidence to transition to a more balanced capital allocation framework," said Bob VanHimbergen, Executive Vice President and CFO of Elanco. "My priority is driving down costs through Elanco Ascend and general and administrative expenses to compensate for inflation. While there is still more to do, we're pleased with the team's disciplined execution to improve working capital management. We're tracking ahead of schedule toward our cumulative free cash flow target of $1 billion from 2026 to 2028, with free cash flow reaching $362 million as of the end of the third quarter and making continued progress toward our long-term margin goals."

The timing, manner and amount of repurchases will depend on a variety of factors, including market conditions, stock price, alternative capital deployment opportunities, and applicable regulatory requirements. The program does not obligate the company to acquire any specific dollar amount or number of shares and may be modified, suspended, or discontinued at any time without prior notice.

About Elanco
Elanco Animal Health Incorporated (NYSE: ELAN) is a global leader in animal health dedicated to innovating and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets, creating value for farmers, pet owners, veterinarians, stakeholders and society as a whole. With 70 years of animal health heritage, we are committed to breaking boundaries and going beyond to help our customers improve the health of animals in their care, while also making a meaningful impact on our local and global communities. At Elanco, we are driven by our vision of Food and Companionship Enriching Life and our purpose – all to Go Beyond for Animals, Customers, Society and Our People. Learn more at www.elanco.com.

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / American Critical Minerals Corp. ("American Critical Minerals" or the "Company") (CSE:KCLI)(OTCQB:APCOF)(Frankfurt:2P3) is pleased to announce that it has received assay results from the Duma Point AP-S-02 well, at the Company's Green River Project located 20 miles northwest of Moab, Utah. The highest-grade assay results returned a composite grade of 42.94 weight per cent ("wt.%") KCl over 2.1 metres ("m") (7 feet) within the Cycle 5 potash member. Geochemical assay data confirm robust potash bed thicknesses and grades, underscoring the high-grade characteristic of the potash mineralization within this area of the Green River Project and the Paradox Basin.

HIGHLIGHTS

  • Assay results and downhole wireline geophysical logs returned a composite grade of 38.51 wt.% KCl over 6.55m or 21.5 feet within the Cycle 5 potash member. High-grade potash with meaningful thickness has now been confirmed at the Green River Project.
  • Results represent an 11% increase in thickness and a 51% increase in grade compared with the historic Quintana Fed 1-1 well located 600m (~ 2,000 feet) east-northeast of the current well 1 .
  • Includes a high composite grade intersection of 42.94 wt.% over 2.1m (6.9 feet).
  • The presence and continuity of sylvite mineralization within the Cycle 5 potash bed now de-risks the historical potash data reported on and available from within the Green River Project.
  • Potash results compare favorably to reported grades from the nearby Moab Solution Mine which produces potash from the same Cycle 5 potash bed 5 .
  • Potash results from the inaugural well on the Green River Project have delivered one of the highest-grade potash intersections globally.

Dean Pekeski, President and CEO stated, "Having completed our inaugural drill program at the Green River Project and we are extremely happy with the results. The potash results are exceptional and highlight the strong pedigree we believed exists within this Property. The significant improvement in both potash grade and thickness versus what was drilled historically validates our targeting exercise and bodes well for future resource delineation. This is a defining moment for our Company and represents the first step in moving this Project forward. Planning for an additional 1-2 wells will commence now with the goal being to generate an NI 43-101 compliant resource and Scoping Study. The Green River Project is progressing while the United States recognizes that critical need for secure fertilizer supply chains."

The Duma Point AP-S-02 Well

The purpose of the Duma Point AP-S-02 well (the "well") was to validate historic drill data and test, through coring and brine sampling, the key Paradox formation potash horizons as well as the clastic brine-bearing zones for lithium and bromine in the Paradox and Leadville formations. Figure 1 shows the location of the Duma Point AP-S-02 well.

Figure 1. - Location map showing the Duma Point AP-S-02 well

Coring operations targeting the Cycle 5 potash member commenced at a depth of 1,741m (5,712 feet) below surface. The core run was planned to recover 45.72m (150 feet) of 4-inch drill core. Due to tight hole conditions causing core loss, core recovery was limited to 25.25m (82.85 feet) with the bottom 20.47 metres (67.15 feet) being lost in the hole. The cored interval did successfully recover 5.54m (18.17 feet) of sylvite mineralization from the Cycle 5 potash member.

To complement the core recovery and aquifer identification, the Company acquired a comprehensive suite of downhole wireline geophysical logs ( "e-logs") to characterize the subsurface stratigraphy and support interpretation of the targeted potash and brine bearing intervals 6 .

The Duma Point AP-S-02 reached a total depth of 2,818 metres (9,245 feet). The well has been cemented and abandoned according to requirements and stipulations found within the State permit for the well, and the drill rig was demobilized on September 25, 2026.

Potash Results

In total, 5.54m (18.17 feet) of sylvite mineralized drill core from the Cycle 5 potash member was recovered (see Figure 2 and Table 1). The downhole wireline geophysical logs show that 1.01m (3.33 feet) of potash mineralized core was lost, meaning that the Cycle 5 potash intersection cut by the well was 6.55m (21.5 feet). In the absence of assays from the lost section of Cycle 5 potash core, downhole wireline geophysical logs results were used to determine the potash content for that interval. 6 There was a strong correlation between the assay results and the downhole wireline geophysical logs for the cored interval.

The vertical well was drilled at Lat: 38.749405, Long: -110.0044758. Based on downhole directional drilling tests and the vertical nature of the stratigraphy interpreted from seismic data the samples are believed to represent true thickness. The 5,794.85-to-5,798.18-foot interval was dropped/lost. Results for this interval are reported from e-logs.

The drill core and completed wireline data confirmed the presence of the Cycle 5 potash unit consistent with historic drilling results from the Quintana Fed 1-1 well, located approximately 0.6 kilometres (~ 2,000 feet) east-northeast of the current well. The Quintana Fed 1-1 well intersected the Cycle 5 potash bed reporting a grade of 24.3% eKCl from elogs over a thickness of 5.9m (19.4 feet).

Recovered core was logged, photographed, sampled, and transported from Rapid City to the Saskatchewan Research Council laboratories in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, for geochemical analysis. Twenty-one halved core samples were collected and shipped under the supervision of qualified independent geological personnel for analysis using industry-standard procedures. Quality assurance and quality control protocols included the insertion of blanks, standards, and duplicate samples throughout the sampling program. Assays were completed along the entire length of recovered core. Core was also retained for future geo-mechanical testing.

Assays from the recovered drill core returned a composite grade of 35.4 wt.% KCl over 5.54m (18.17 feet) in the Cycle 5 potash member assuming a 5% K 2 O cut-off. Composite carnallite and insoluble content was very low with each reporting <0.1 wt.% and <1.0 wt.% respectively. Included in this assayed interval was a high-grade interval which comprised 2.1m (7 feet) of potash core with a composite grade of 42.94 wt.% KCl (5,780 to 5,787 feet). Table 1 summarizes the assay results from this drill hole.

Figure 2. - Duma Point AP-S-02 photograph of high-grade zone drill core

Adjusting for the lost drill core, the Duma Point AP-S-02 assays and downhole wireline geophysical logs returned a composite grade of 38.51 wt.% KCl over 6.55m (21.5 feet) within the Cycle 5 potash member.

Geochemical assay data and grade interpretations from the e-logs confirm robust potash bed thicknesses and grades, underscoring the high-grade character of mineralization within this area of the Green River Project and Paradox Basin. Figure 3 shows how the grade from the Duma Point AP-S-02 well compares with average KCl grades from other potash projects in North America. The intersection reported represents an 11% increase in thickness and a 51% increase in grade compared with the historical e-logs from the Quintana Fed 1-1 well.

Lithium and Bromine Aquifers

Two short-duration drill stem packer tests were completed targeting the Leadville Formation limestone unit (2,670 to 2,815 m or 8,760.2 to 9,236 feet), and lower clastic units of the Paradox Formation (2,144 to 2,181m or 7,035 to 7,155 feet). Although brine was successfully sampled from the Leadville Formation test, meaningful lithium and bromine results were not obtained. Future longer duration pumping tests could provide different results. The sample collected from the Paradox Formation was contaminated with drilling fluids/mud and deemed to be inconclusive. Given these results and the high-cost nature of drilling to these depths, the Company will re-evaluate future drilling and sampling programs within these deep zones.

About American Critical Minerals' Green River Potash and Lithium Project

The Green River Project is situated within Utah's highly productive Paradox Basin, located 20 miles northwest of Moab, Utah. It has significant logistical advantages including close proximity to major rail hubs, airport, roads, water, towns, and labour markets. It also benefits from close proximity to the agricultural and industrial heartland of America and numerous potential end-users for its products.

The history of oil and gas production across the Paradox Basin provides geologic data from historic wells across the Project, and the wider Basin, validating and de-risking the potential for high grade potash and large amounts of contained lithium. Wells in and around the project reported lithium up to 500 ppm, bromine up to 6,100 ppm and boron up to 1,260 ppm (Gilbride & Santos, 2012). This data is reinforced by nearby potash production and the advanced stage of neighbouring lithium projects. The Paradox Basin is believed to be one of the biggest sources of lithium brines in the United States. (Source: AnsonFastmarketsPresentation- https://wcsecure.weblink.com.au/pdf/ASN/02823465.pdf ) .1

The Company has disclosed targets for further exploration at the Green River Project consisting of 500 million to 950 million tonnes of sylvinite (the most important source for the production of potash in North America) 4 grading from 12% to 18% potassium oxide based on elog (eK2O=19% to 29% potassium chloride based on elog (eKCl)). Its target for further exploration for Lithium and Bromine is 2.1 billion cubic meters brine volume grading 71.6 to 216.3 ppm Li and 3,656 to 4,741 ppm Br. 2

The Company holds a 100% interest in eleven SITLA mineral and minerals salt leases covering approximately 7,050 acres, 1,094 federal lithium brine claims (BLM Placer Claims) covering 21,150 acres, and 11 federal (BLM) potash prospecting permits covering approximately 25,480 acres. Through these leases, permits and claims the Company has the ability to explore for potash, lithium, and potential by-products across the entire Green River Project (approx. 32,530 acres). The Company is authorized to drill a total of 7 drill holes across the Green River Project.

America's largest potash company and only U.S. domestic potash producer currently produces potash from its nearby Moab Solution Mine, which the Company believes provides strong evidence of stratigraphic continuity within this part of the Paradox Basin 5 . Anson Resources Ltd. has advanced lithium development projects contiguous to the northern boundary of our Green River Project and neighbouring to the south. 5 Anson has a large initial resource, robust definitive feasibility study and has recently completed successful piloting operations through its partnership with Koch Technology Solutions, as well as an offtake agreement with LG Energy Solution. The Anson exploration targets encompass the combined Mississippian Leadville Formation and the Pennsylvanian Paradox Formation brine-bearing clastic layers, which also underlie American Critical Minerals' entire project area (www.ansonresources.com). 3

The United States imports more than 90% of its potash demand (U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries, January 2025). In November 2025, the Department of Interior added potash to its list of Critical Minerals which already includes lithium. Recent market estimates suggest that the global potash market is over US$50 billion annually and growing at a compound annual growth rate ("CAGR") of close to 5%. Annual lithium demand is now estimated to be over 1 million tonnes globally and continuing to grow rapidly. 4

Schlumberger furthered this work and related log response to apparent K 2 O content. The established methodology developed by Schlumberger calculates K 2 O% combining gamma ray American Petroleum Institute (API) units and correcting to hole diameter (from caliper logs) and mud weight. Experience has shown good agreement between the estimation when compared with assay data.

HONG KONG--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE: BABA and HKEX: 9988 (HKD Counter) and 89988 (RMB Counter), “Alibaba” or “Alibaba Group”) today announced its financial results for the quarter and the six months ended September 30, 2026.

“Our full-stack AI capabilities continue to improve commercialization and delivered a strong quarter. Growth in Alibaba Cloud’s recurring revenue from external customers was 67%, which drove an acceleration of overall cloud revenue growth with significantly improving profitability. AI-related product revenue delivered triple-digit growth for the thirteenth consecutive quarter. We recently announced comprehensive upgrades spanning proprietary chips, supernode architecture, agent-native cloud infrastructure, AI models and agents. Notably, T-Head unveiled its next-generation Zhenwu V900 AI chip. In our consumption business, Alibaba E-commerce Group’s profitability improved significantly. Quick commerce continued to narrow its losses substantially while maintaining market share,” said Eddie Wu, Chief Executive Officer of Alibaba Group. “We will continue to bring technological innovations to our comprehensive AI stack to meet the strong and diverse AI demands across industries.”

“This quarter, our business delivered strong growth in both revenue and earnings because of our strategic focus on AI + Cloud growth and profit sustainability in Alibaba E-commerce Group. Cloud segment revenue growth continued to accelerate, with quality earnings further driving EBITA margin up to 14.5%. The e-commerce segment delivered significant EBITA growth, driven by improving unit economics in quick commerce and solid growth of marketplace e-commerce,” said Toby Xu, Chief Financial Officer of Alibaba Group. “As AI monetization continues to ramp up, we will maintain disciplined investments in AI capabilities with a focus on return on invested capital while targeting to achieve positive free cash flow.”

BUSINESS HIGHLIGHTS

In the quarter ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenue was RMB271,519 million (US$40,498 million), an increase of 10% year-over-year.
  • AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue increased by 53% year-over-year. Revenue from external customers increased by 64% year-over-year, primarily attributable to a 67% growth in recurring revenue from external customers (excluding compute equipment solutions revenue), largely driven by the increasing adoption of AI-related products.
  • Customer management revenue decreased by 5% year-over-year. Excluding the contra revenue impact from the new business development program, customer management revenue on a like-for-like basis would have grown by 1% year-over-year.
  • Income from operations was RMB29,116 million (US$4,343 million), an increase of 443% year-over-year, primarily due to the increase in adjusted EBITA. Adjusted EBITA, a non-GAAP measurement, increased 260% year-over-year to RMB32,636 million (US$4,868 million), primarily attributable to the improved operating results in Taobao Instant Commerce and Cloud business, as well as operating efficiencies across various businesses, partly offset by our increased investment in technology.
  • Net income attributable to ordinary shareholders was RMB64,535 million (US$9,626 million). Net income was RMB64,420 million (US$9,608 million), an increase of 213% year-over-year, primarily attributable to the increase in net investment income and income from operations. Non-GAAP net income in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was RMB19,909 million (US$2,969 million), an increase of 92% compared to RMB10,352 million in the same quarter of 2025.
  • Diluted earnings per ADS was RMB25.94 (US$3.87). Diluted earnings per share was RMB3.24 (US$0.48 or HK$3.78). Non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS was RMB8.10 (US$1.21), an increase of 86% year-over-year. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share was RMB1.01 (US$0.15 or HK$1.18), an increase of 86% year-over-year.
  • Net cash provided by operating activities was RMB15,690 million (US$2,340 million), an increase of 55% compared to RMB10,099 million in the same quarter of 2025. Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measurement of liquidity, was an outflow of RMB34,472 million (US$5,142 million), compared to an outflow of RMB21,840 million in the same quarter of 2025. The decrease in free cash flow was mainly attributed to the increase in our cloud infrastructure expenditure, partly offset by reduced losses in Taobao Instant Commerce and increased customer prepayments for our cloud services. As of September 30, 2026, our cash and other liquid investments(1) were RMB487,929 million (US$72,776 million).

In the six months ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenue was RMB540,472 million (US$80,613 million), an increase of 9% year-over-year.
  • AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue increased by 49% year-over-year. Revenue from external customers increased by 56% year-over-year, primarily attributable to a 54% growth in recurring revenue from external customers (excluding compute equipment solutions revenue), which was largely driven by the increasing adoption of AI-related products.
  • Customer management revenue decreased by 6% year-over-year. Excluding the contra revenue impact from the new business development program, customer management revenue on a like-for-like basis would have grown by 1% year-over-year.
  • Income from operations was RMB44,277 million (US$6,604 million), an increase of 10% year-over-year, primarily due to the increase in adjusted EBITA, partly offset by the increase in impairment of goodwill, and a provision(2) recorded this year. Adjusted EBITA, a non-GAAP measurement, increased 25% year-over-year to RMB59,965 million (US$8,944 million), primarily attributable to the improved operating results in Taobao Instant Commerce and Cloud business, as well as operating efficiencies across various businesses, partly offset by our increased investment in technology.
  • Net income attributable to ordinary shareholders was RMB75,072 million (US$11,197 million). Net income was RMB74,864 million (US$11,166 million), an increase of 19% year-over-year, primarily attributable to the increase in net investment income and income from operations. Non-GAAP net income was RMB40,624 million (US$6,059 million), a decrease of 7% compared to RMB43,862 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Diluted earnings per ADS was RMB29.91 (US$4.46). Diluted earnings per share was RMB3.74 (US$0.56 or HK$4.36). Non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS was RMB16.62 (US$2.48), a decrease of 13% year-over-year. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share was RMB2.08 (US$0.31 or HK$2.42), a decrease of 13% year-over-year.
  • Net cash provided by operating activities was RMB38,635 million (US$5,763 million), an increase of 26% compared to RMB30,771 million in the same period of 2025. Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measurement of liquidity, was an outflow of RMB79,142 million (US$11,804 million), compared to an outflow of RMB40,655 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease in free cash flow was mainly attributed to the increase in our cloud infrastructure expenditure, partly offset by reduced losses in Taobao Instant Commerce and increased customer prepayments for our cloud services. As of September 30, 2026, our cash and other liquid investments(1) were RMB487,929 million (US$72,776 million).

BUSINESS AND STRATEGIC UPDATES

Alibaba E-commerce Group

During the quarter, we sustained revenue stability with CMR decreasing 5% year-over-year and growing 1% on a like-for-like basis if the contra revenue impact from the new business development program were excluded. Adjusted EBITA of the group achieved 243% year-over-year growth this quarter, primarily driven by a significant loss reduction in the China Quick Commerce business. In addition, our China E-commerce business contributed to stable operating profit and the Global Wholesale business delivered strong profits, while we reduced losses in the International E-commerce business.

We have continued to advance our strategic priorities of unlocking significant synergies across our domestic and cross-border businesses, and deepening the integration of AI capabilities across our e-commerce platforms. Recent progress includes the integration of management across our domestic and international wholesale businesses, as well as the launch of QwenWork E-commerce for merchants, an AI product powered by our agentic AI capabilities, in October.

QwenWork E-commerce is integrated into QwenWork, our one-stop AI agent platform, and is designed to automate end-to-end merchant workflows, including store operations, business analytics, advertising and customer service. Leveraging our existing merchant tools, it connects directly to Taobao and Tmall data and will further support data access across other platforms, enabling more seamless cross-platform operations. In addition, by leveraging Qwen model family’s advanced multimodal capabilities, we are able to better understand complex consumer needs and deliver more relevant product recommendations with knowledge-based reasoning. These enhanced capabilities have driven a notable increase in general knowledge-related queries, creating more opportunities to identify latent consumer demand, facilitate product discovery, and drive sales conversion.

In our China Quick Commerce business, Taobao Instant Commerce continued to improve its unit economics quarter-over-quarter while maintaining market share. This reflected higher average order value, as we further improved the order mix through an increasing focus on high-value food and non-food categories. Meanwhile, Freshippo maintained its robust growth across online and offline channels, driven by deeper collaboration with Taobao Instant Commerce and the expansion of its multi-format store network that offers differentiated products to diverse demographics.

The number of 88VIP members, our highest spending consumer group, continued to increase by double digits year-over-year to approximately 66 million as of September 30, 2026. The ARPU of new 88VIP members, defined as those who joined the membership program within the past year, increased significantly year-over-year during the 11.11 Global Shopping Festival. We remain focused on the growth and retention of 88VIP members through enhanced value proposition to our most valued customers.

Xianyu is China’s leading consumer-to-consumer community and marketplace for idle goods. It makes buying and selling more convenient for consumers and small businesses through AI-powered features including smart pricing, automated product listing descriptions and precise buyer targeting, as well as consignment services. This quarter, Xianyu continued its strong growth momentum, with daily active users and paid orders up 23% and 29% year-over-year, respectively.

AI Cloud and Compute Services

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, revenue from AI Cloud and Compute Services was RMB60,973 million (US$9,094 million), a 53% increase from the same quarter last year. The growth of revenue from external customers accelerated to 64% year-over-year. The growth of recurring revenue from external customers, which excludes compute equipment solutions revenue, also accelerated to 67% year-over-year. In particular, AI-related product revenue continued to show strong momentum, achieving RMB17,918 million (US$2,673 million) and delivering the thirteenth consecutive quarter of triple-digit year-over-year growth. The strong growth reflected broad-based demand for our AI + Cloud services. Beyond training and inference workloads at AI labs, customers across the internet, automotive, embodied AI, financial services and biotechnology sectors rapidly expanded their use of our cloud services to support innovation and grow their business.

Cloud

Alibaba Cloud continued to strengthen our market-leading full-stack AI capabilities, as demonstrated by the comprehensive upgrades unveiled at the Apsara Conference in September, spanning proprietary chips, supernode architecture, agent-native cloud infrastructure, AI models and agents. These advancements across our co-designed and integrated stack have accelerated enterprise adoption and deeper integration into core business workflows, enabling us to capitalize on increasingly diverse demand across industries.

Our ability to empower enterprise AI adoption has earned notable recognition in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Strategic Cloud Platform Services, a report that comprehensively evaluates how cloud service providers support the entire enterprise cloud lifecycle. Alibaba Cloud was named a Leader in the highest quadrant, making it the first and only Asia-Pacific provider to receive this distinction.

Chip Design – T-Head Semiconductor (“T-Head”)

By rapidly advancing its portfolio of proprietary chips and software, T-Head further strengthened the infrastructure foundation underpinning our AI capabilities.

At the Apsara Conference in September, we unveiled the Zhenwu V900, our next-generation AI chip for training and inference, with commercial release scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. Built on our proprietary parallel computing architecture, the Zhenwu V900 delivers significant performance improvements over its predecessor, the Zhenwu M890. We also open-sourced T-Head SAIL, the software stack for Zhenwu chips, to simplify application migration, expand developer adoption, and strengthen compatibility with mainstream AI frameworks.

In addition, we launched the Zhenwu M890 supernode instance in August, marking the introduction of China’s first supernode architecture capable of supporting inference for models with more than two trillion parameters. At the Apsara Conference, we also showcased our next-generation supernode product, which integrates the Zhenwu V900 with other proprietary interconnect, networking, and storage chips, and is scheduled for launch in the first quarter of 2027.

AI Labs and Applications

Model

We continued to advance our comprehensive model portfolio, with a primary focus on foundation models, while enhancing capabilities across video, audio, image and music. This demonstrates our industry leadership and rapid pace of iteration.

Recently, we launched Qwen4-Max, built on the new mixture-of-experts architecture with 2.4 trillion backbone parameters and native visual capabilities. Qwen4-Max advances productivity and token efficiency, delivering stronger long-horizon task execution across industries, including manufacturing, game development, healthcare, and frontier scientific research.

QwenWork

Our agentic platform QwenWork continued to gain traction across industries, driven by ongoing enhancements to its enterprise capabilities. At the Apsara Conference in September, we launched Enterprise Context, a solution that continuously organizes and updates enterprise information and knowledge across company documents, meeting records and internal communications. It enables AI agents to access company-specific information and execute tasks based on organizational knowledge and workflows.

Qwen App

Qwen app for individual users now provides personalized assistance for tasks across more than 20 service categories, including shopping, local services, travel, work, learning, personal finance and health, leveraging Alibaba’s ecosystem and third-party partnerships. In October, we launched Qwen Go!, a cloud-based personal agent embedded within the Qwen app. Qwen Go! autonomously executes multi-step tasks across platforms, while retaining contextual information and user preferences over time to deliver increasingly personalized assistance across everyday activities.

All Others

Our store guide and mapping platform Amap offers consumers one-stop access to services such as navigation, to-destination services and ride-hailing. On October 1, 2026, the first day of National Day holiday in China, Amap recorded an all-time high of approximately 370 million peak daily active users. Leveraging Amap Street Stars, a feature that provides a trust-based rating system to support users’ consumption decisions, Amap has strengthened its mindshare in local services across consumption use cases, including dining, tourist attractions and seasonal activities.

Share Repurchases

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, we repurchased a total of 17.95 million ordinary shares (equivalent to approximately 2.24 million ADSs) for a total of US$221 million. These purchases were made in the U.S. market under our share repurchase program.

Capital Expenditures

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, capital expenditures were RMB50,477 million (US$7,529 million), an increase of 60% compared to RMB31,501 million in the same quarter of 2025, due to continued investments in AI infrastructure to meet strong and accelerating customer demand. The significant year-over-year increase was due to an acceleration in scaling compute capacity, higher pricing of a broad range of chip components, an increase in CPU-compute capacity driven by anticipated growing customer adoption of AI agents, and fluctuations in procurement cycles.

In addition to training and inference demand from AI Labs, we continue to see robust demand from customers in China’s emerging innovation economy, including electric vehicles (EVs), embodied AI, and biotechnology. Scale is becoming an increasingly critical competitive advantage in cloud computing, providing us with orchestration flexibility, operating efficiency and cost advantages. By investing in infrastructure today, we aim to extend our scale leadership, strengthen our supply chain and reinforce our long-term competitive position.

(i) Segment revenue

Revenue from our AI Cloud and Compute Services in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was RMB60,973 million (US$9,094 million), an increase of 53% compared to RMB39,914 million in the same quarter of 2025. Revenue from external customers increased by 64% year-over-year, primarily attributable to a 67% growth in recurring revenue, which was largely driven by the increasing adoption of AI-related products. NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES

To supplement our consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP, we use the following non-GAAP financial measures: for our consolidated results, adjusted EBITDA (including adjusted EBITDA margin), adjusted EBITA (including adjusted EBITA margin), non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share/ADS and free cash flow. For more information on these non-GAAP financial measures, please refer to the table captioned “Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Measures to the Nearest Comparable U.S. GAAP Measures” in this results announcement.

We believe that adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITA, non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share/ADS help identify underlying trends in our business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain income or expenses that we include in income from operations, net income and diluted earnings per share/ADS. We believe that these non-GAAP measures provide useful information about our core operating results, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by our management in its financial and operational decision-making. We present three different income measures, namely adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITA and non-GAAP net income in order to provide more information and greater transparency to investors about our operating results.

We consider free cash flow to be a liquidity measure that provides useful information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated by our business that can be used for strategic corporate transactions, including investing in our new business initiatives, making strategic investments and acquisitions and strengthening our balance sheet.

Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITA, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share/ADS and free cash flow should not be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to income from operations, net income, diluted earnings per share/ADS, cash flows or any other measure of performance or as an indicator of our operating performance. These non-GAAP financial measures presented here do not have standardized meanings prescribed by U.S. GAAP and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies. Other companies may calculate similarly titled measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures to our data.

Adjusted EBITDA represents net income before interest and investment income, net, interest expense, other income (expense), net, income tax expenses, share of results of equity method investees, certain non-cash expenses, consisting of share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, impairment of goodwill, depreciation and impairment of property and equipment, and operating lease cost relating to land use rights, and others (including provision in relation to matters outside the ordinary course of business), which we do not believe are reflective of our core operating performance during the periods presented.

Adjusted EBITA represents net income before interest and investment income, net, interest expense, other income (expense), net, income tax expenses, share of results of equity method investees, certain non-cash expenses, consisting of share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, impairment of goodwill, and others (including provision in relation to matters outside the ordinary course of business), which we do not believe are reflective of our core operating performance during the periods presented.

Non-GAAP net income represents net income before non-cash share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, gain or loss on deemed disposals/disposals/revaluation of investments, impairment of goodwill and investments, and others (including provision in relation to matters outside the ordinary course of business), and adjustments for the tax effects.

Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share represents non-GAAP net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by the weighted average number of outstanding ordinary shares, in each case for computing non-GAAP diluted earnings per share on a diluted basis. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS represents non-GAAP diluted earnings per share after adjusting for the ordinary share-to-ADS ratio.

Free cash flow represents net cash provided by operating activities as presented in our consolidated cash flow statement less purchases of property and equipment (excluding acquisition of land use rights and construction in progress relating to office campuses) and intangible assets (excluding those acquired through acquisitions), as well as adjustments to exclude from net cash provided by operating activities the buyer protection fund deposits from merchants on our marketplaces. We deduct certain items of cash flows from investing activities in order to provide greater transparency into cash flow from our revenue-generating business operations. We exclude “acquisition of land use rights and construction in progress relating to office campuses” because the office campuses are used by us for corporate and administrative purposes and are not directly related to our revenue-generating business operations. We also exclude buyer protection fund deposits from merchants on our marketplaces because these deposits are restricted for the purpose of compensating buyers for claims against merchants.

Key Terms

ebitafinancial
EBITA stands for Earnings Before Interest, Taxes and Amortization and measures a company’s profit from operations after removing the effects of financing, tax rules and amortization charges. Investors use it to compare underlying business performance across firms by focusing on the company’s core ability to generate cash, like judging a car’s engine power before accounting for fuel costs, loan payments and bookkeeping adjustments.
non-gaapfinancial
Non-GAAP refers to financial measures that companies use to show their earnings or performance without including certain expenses or income that are often added back to give a different picture. It matters because it can make a company's results look better or more favorable, but it may also hide important costs, so investors need to look at both GAAP (official rules) and non-GAAP numbers to get a full understanding.

free cash flowfinancial
Free cash flow is the amount of money a company has left over after paying all its expenses and investing in its business, like buying equipment or updating facilities. It shows how much cash is available to reward shareholders, pay down debt, or save for future growth. This helps investors understand if a company is financially healthy and able to grow.

adsfinancial
Ads are paid promotional messages a company places across media — online, on TV, in print, or on social platforms — to attract customers, explain products, or shape public perception. For investors, ads matter because they drive sales growth, affect how much a company must spend to win customers, and influence brand strength and long-term value. Ads can also create regulatory or reputational risk if claims are misleading, which can affect profits and stock price.

ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / LASE Corp. (NASDAQ:LASE), an emerging laser technology company developing laser and directed-energy solutions for the defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and industrial markets ("LASE" or the "Company"), today announced that it will premiere its Quantum Bullet™ anti-drone platform at Counter Unmanned Aircraft System ("UAS") Technology USA, taking place November 30 through December 2, 2026, in Washington, D.C., where Dmitri Nikitin, Executive Chairman of LASE Corp., will also present as a featured speaker.

This event brings together military, government and industry leaders to address the rapidly evolving threat posed by unmanned aerial systems and the technologies being developed to defeat them. This year's conference speakers include senior representatives of Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401), the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, the U.S. Army, the Air Force Research Laboratory, U.S. Northern Command and the Department of Homeland Security. Last year's conference drew attendees from more than a dozen countries, NATO, and allied ministries of defense, as well as leading defense contractors.

This premiere complements the Company's previously announced introduction of Quantum Bullet™ at the Interservice/Industry Training, Simulation and Education Conference (I/ITSEC), taking place November 30 through December 3, 2026, in Orlando, Florida.

The Quantum Bullet™ product line includes the Company's Laser Shield Anti-Drone ("LSAD") Series, a modular directed-energy platform being developed to address Group 1 and Group 2 drone threats. LSAD is designed to combine proprietary laser-based counter-drone capabilities with multi-sensor detection, tracking, targeting and command-and-control ("C2") systems supplied by LASE and its integration partners, supporting either standalone deployment or integration into multilayered air-defense networks.

LASE is developing LSAD as a modular offering that can be configured with different laser and power capabilities for different tactical scenarios. Its Dazzler configuration is intended to disrupt the optical and LIDAR sensors of Group 1 and Group 2 drones, while higher-energy palletized and crawler configurations, the latter designed for rapid all-terrain deployment, are being developed for destructive engagement of drone threats. Development, integration, testing and customer evaluation remain necessary before commercialization.

Dmitri Nikitin, Executive Chairman of LASE Corp said, "What we have developed with Quantum Bullet™ is a fundamentally different approach to counter-drone defense. It is designed to deliver the precision, effectiveness and cost efficiency needed to address one of the military's most urgent and widespread threats: Group 1 and Group 2 drones. But what makes Quantum Bullet™ particularly compelling is its versatility. It is not simply a standalone weapon. It is a modular, mobile and integrated defense platform designed to operate independently or as part of a larger, layered defense system."

Dmitri Nikitin continued, "We believe the future of counter-drone defense will depend on technologies that work together, adapt to evolving threats and can be deployed wherever our military needs them. That is exactly what we are building with Quantum Bullet™.

Mr. Nikitin, the Company's founder, brings more than three decades of experience in laser technology innovation spanning marking, cutting, welding, cleaning, glass separation and semiconductor processing. He co-developed the world's first high-power fiber laser cutting system and developed a first-of-its-kind mobile fiber-laser platform for military mine-clearing applications. Mr. Nikitin holds an engineering degree in industrial electronics and quantum mechanics from Moscow Power Engineering University and a Ph.D. from the Ministry of Electronics Industry of the USSR, and he is a named inventor on three patent applications relating to Bulk-to-Shape technology.

Quantum Bullet™ is a registered trademark with the USPTO.

For more information on LASE Corp. and its brands, please visit www.lase.com.

About LASE Corp.

LASE Corp. (NASDAQ:LASE), formerly Laser Photonics Corporation, is an emerging laser technology company developing laser and directed-energy solutions for the defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and industrial markets. Through internal development, strategic acquisitions and partnerships, LASE intends to expand its technology portfolio, strengthen its advanced manufacturing capabilities and scale the enterprise profitably.

Fiscal Year 2026 Highlights

The Company's revenue increased 325.2% to $58.8 million, principally reflecting the first full fiscal year of Nautical Ventures Group Inc. ("Nautical Ventures") operations.

Nautical Ventures' floor-plan financing decreased 84.5% to $5.0 million, a reduction of $27.5 million from the prior year.

Consolidated inventories decreased by $22.4 million to $14.5 million, reflecting deliberate actions to convert aging inventory into cash and reduce related borrowing.

The Company generated $3.2 million in operating cash flow, an improvement of $12.4 million year over year, principally driven by inventory reductions.

Vision Marine segment revenue increased to $1.55 million, compared with $1.00 million in fiscal 2025.

BOISBRIAND, QC, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vision Marine Technologies Inc. (Nasdaq: VMAR) ("Vision Marine" or the "Company") today reported its audited financial results for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2026, following the filing of its Annual Report on Form 10-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") on November 18, 2026. Unless otherwise indicated, all amounts are in U.S. dollars. Fiscal 2025 comparative financial information has been adjusted to U.S. GAAP as presented in the Company's annual report.

"Fiscal 2026 marked an important year in Vision Marine's evolution, with Nautical Ventures providing a significantly expanded commercial platform and our teams making substantial progress in inventory and capital management," said Alexandre Mongeon, Chief Executive Officer of Vision Marine. "We took decisive action to reduce inventory, generate cash and substantially lower floor-plan borrowing. These accomplishments reflect our focus on financial discipline and position us to pursue opportunities across our marine retail, service and electric propulsion businesses."

"We enter fiscal 2027 with substantially less inventory-related borrowing and a clear focus on our core marine operations. Nautical Ventures' customer relationships, experienced sales teams and service and marina capabilities provide the commercial foundation for our next phase. Looking ahead, we are focused on aligning inventory purchases with customer demand, developing service and marina revenue opportunities and taking a disciplined approach to growth. Growth in Vision Marine's own sales adds to our progress as we pursue opportunities to expand sales of E-Motion™-equipped boats through Nautical Ventures."

Fiscal Year Ended August 31, 2026, Results

Revenue totaled $58.82 million, an increase of $45.0 million, or 325.2%, compared with $13.83 million in fiscal 2025. The increase principally reflects the inclusion of a full year of Nautical Ventures operations, compared with consolidation from the June 20, 2025, acquisition date in the prior year.

Nautical Ventures generated $57.27 million in revenue, compared with $12.84 million in fiscal 2025. The Vision Marine segment generated $1.55 million in revenue, compared with $1.00 million a year earlier.

Gross profit totaled $13.91 million, compared with $4.77 million in fiscal 2025. Gross profit margin was 23.6%, compared with 34.5%. The margin decline reflected, in part, deliberate sales of aging and excess inventory at reduced margins to release working capital, repay floor-plan financing and reduce associated carrying costs.

Operating loss was $18.97 million, compared with $25.79 million in fiscal 2025. The prior year included a $15.08 million goodwill impairment that did not recur in fiscal 2026. This item, together with the different periods of Nautical Ventures consolidation, materially affects the year-over-year comparison.

Net loss totaled $21.45 million, compared with $21.23 million in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 results included a full year of Nautical Ventures expenses, reduced margins from inventory liquidation, a $1.09 million battery-supplier advance impairment and a $1.0 million litigation-related charge. In addition to the goodwill impairment, fiscal 2025 included significant non-cash gains on derivative liabilities and convertible-note fair-value changes that did not recur at comparable levels in fiscal 2026.

Basic and diluted loss per share was $202.54, compared with $97,366.39 for fiscal 2025. The substantial year-over-year decrease in reported loss per share, despite relatively comparable net losses, was primarily attributable to the substantial increase in the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding following the Company's equity financing activities during fiscal 2026. Per-share amounts have been adjusted to reflect the reverse stock splits described in the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flow

"Our fiscal 2026 results demonstrate meaningful progress in working-capital management and financial discipline," said Raffi Sossoyan, Chief Financial Officer. "By converting inventory into cash, we generated positive operating cash flow and significantly reduced our floor-plan financing obligations. These actions have reduced our inventory-related financing exposure and strengthened our focus on liquidity management. As we enter fiscal 2027, our priorities remain disciplined capital allocation, cash preservation and supporting the Company's operating and strategic objectives."

At August 31, 2026, Nautical Ventures' outstanding floor-plan financing was $5.03 million, compared with $32.51 million a year earlier, a reduction of $27.48 million, or 84.5%. Consolidated inventories decreased to $14.51 million from $36.87 million.

Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $3.23 million, compared with $9.13 million used in fiscal 2025. Inventory reductions were the principal contributor to the $12.36 million year-over-year improvement.

Cash and cash equivalents were $6.38 million at year-end, compared with $7.42 million at August 31, 2025. Restricted cash was $1.20 million, compared with nil. Working capital was $10.27 million, compared with $9.55 million. Total assets were $37.08 million, total liabilities were $25.11 million, and shareholders' equity was $11.97 million.

Net cash provided by investing activities was $4.04 million, including approximately $4.38 million in proceeds from related-party real estate transactions. Net cash used in financing activities was $7.11 million, reflecting repayments of floor-plan financing and other obligations, partially offset by proceeds from equity financing and borrowings.

Strategic Business Combination Update

As previously announced on August 24, 2026, Vision Marine entered into a non-binding letter of intent concerning a potential strategic business combination with a privately held company operating in the unmanned and autonomous systems sector, including applications serving defense, government and critical infrastructure markets.

Discussions and due diligence activities relating to the proposed transaction remain ongoing. The Company continues to evaluate the potential transaction and its strategic implications. No definitive agreement has been executed, and any transaction remains subject to satisfactory due diligence, negotiation of definitive terms, financing, applicable approvals and other customary conditions. There can be no assurance that a definitive agreement will be reached or that a transaction will be completed.

Financial Reporting and Liquidity Considerations

As disclosed in the Company's audited consolidated financial statements, conditions and events raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the issuance of those financial statements. The Company continues to manage its liquidity and financing requirements and is undertaking remediation efforts relating to identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting. Certain financing arrangements remain subject to defaults, forbearance agreements and related uncertainties.

Proposed acquisition of remaining 49% eliminates joint venture structure and positions the Project for institutional scale capital

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Bayridge Resources Corp. (CSE: BYRG) (OTCQB: BYRRF) (FSE: O0K) ("Bayridge" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has entered into a binding letter of intent (the "LOI") to acquire the remaining 49% of the issued and outstanding common shares of 1461433 B.C. Ltd. ("Privco") that it does not already own (the "Acquisition"). Privco is the beneficial owner of a 100% interest in the Baker Lake Uranium Project in the Kivalliq Region of Nunavut (the "Project"). Upon completion of the Acquisition, Privco will be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, and the Company will indirectly own a 100% interest in the Project.

Highlights

  • 100% ownership: Upon completion of the Acquisition, Bayridge's indirect interest in the Project will increase from 51% to 100%.

  • Joint venture eliminated: The LOI provides for the waiver of the joint venture arrangements, including the related free-carried interest, contemplated by the November 2025 share purchase agreement.

  • Simplified ownership structure: Full ownership is expected to provide greater flexibility in advancing exploration and evaluating future financing and strategic opportunities for the Project.

  • Institutional-grade structure: A single-owner asset with no minority partner or carried interest gives a simpler profile for institutional investors, uranium-focused funds and potential strategic partners.

  • Substantially all share consideration: The consideration payable to the Vendors (as defined below) will consist of 14,000,000 common shares of the Company. The Company paid Privco a $10,000 non-refundable cash deposit upon execution of the LOI.

  • District-scale land package: 83 contiguous claims covering 619 km², about 60 km south of the town of Baker Lake, in the same Paleoproterozoic uranium district that hosts ATHA's Angilak and Orano's Kiggavik deposits.

Strategic Rationale: Positioning Baker Lake for Institutional Capital

Bayridge acquired its initial 51% interest in Privco on December 11, 2025 pursuant to a share purchase agreement entered into in November 2025 (the "Initial Agreement"). The Initial Agreement contemplated a joint venture arrangement under which the remaining 49% interest would be a free-carried interest until completion of a pre-feasibility study. Completion of the Acquisition would consolidate the Company's ownership of the Project and eliminate the contemplated minority and free-carried interests, providing the Company with sole control over the Project's exploration strategy, budgets and timing.

Management believes that consolidating ownership will simplify the Project's ownership structure and provide greater flexibility in evaluating future financing, strategic investment and partnership opportunities.

Saf Dhillon, President & Chief Executive Officer of Bayridge, commented: "Moving towards a 100% ownership of Baker Lake will be a defining step for Bayridge. When we secured our initial 51% last November, our goal was to build a district-scale uranium position in one of Canada's most prospective and under-explored basins. Consolidating full ownership is intended to give us a clean, single-owner asset with full control over how and when we advance it, which is exactly the profile institutional investors and strategic partners look for. We believe the long-term fundamentals for uranium remain compelling. We thank the Privco shareholders for their continued support and look forward to completing this acquisition promptly."

About the Baker Lake Uranium Project

The Project is an advanced-stage exploration opportunity supported by about 5,500 m of modern drilling, 23.5 km² of detailed surface grids and 7,851 line-km of basin-scale airborne geophysics. At 2025 cost equivalencies, this work represents over $7 million in exploration value (Fugro Airborne Surveys, 2008; Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd., 2006; Pacific Ridge Exploration Ltd., 2007). Early work by Pan Ocean (1960s-1976) and Noranda (1978-1984) identified 20 uranium prospects along 75 km of the Baker Basin unconformity. The 2008 TEMPEST® radiometric and EM survey defined 30 priority targets, most of which remain untested (Fugro Airborne Surveys, 2008).

Pacific Ridge conducted drilling on the Project during 2006 and 2007. Selected historical drill results include:

  • (L7-07-08) 17.3 m of 0.30% U₃O₈
  • (L7-07-10) 10.0 m of 0.35% U₃O₈
  • (L7-07-06) 15.3 m of 0.20% U₃O₈, including 0.9 m of 2.74% U₃O₈
  • (KZ-06-02) 11.5 m of 0.31% U₃O₈, including 5.5 m of 0.56% U₃O₈

All drill intervals represent core lengths; true widths are unknown. Historical surface sampling also returned values of up to 1.83% U₃O₈. The reported maximum surface sample value is not necessarily representative of mineralization across the Project.

The historical exploration results summarized above were previously disclosed in the Company's news release entitled "Bayridge Resources Signs Definitive Agreement on Baker Lake Uranium Project in Nunavut" dated November 24, 2025, filed under the Company's profile on SEDAR+. Readers are referred to that news release, including its appendices, for supporting information concerning drill hole locations and orientations, sampling, sample preparation, analytical methods and quality assurance and quality control procedures.

Readers are also referred to the Company's most recently-filed technical report, a copy of which may be obtained under the Company's profile at www.sedarplus.ca, for a further discussion of the Company's QA/QC and data verification processes and procedures.

Terms of the Acquisition

The LOI was entered into between the Company and Privco and contemplates the acquisition by the Company of 915,327 common shares of Privco, representing the remaining 49% of Privco's issued and outstanding common shares, from the holders thereof (the "Vendors"). The Vendors are not parties to the LOI and are not bound to sell their shares solely by virtue of the LOI. Completion of the Acquisition requires all Vendors to execute a definitive share purchase agreement among the Company, Privco and the Vendors (the "Definitive Agreement"). Upon completion of the Acquisition, the Company will own all of the issued and outstanding shares of Privco.

As consideration for the shares of Privco to be acquired, the Company will issue an aggregate of 14,000,000 common shares of the Company (the "Consideration Shares"), to be allocated among the Vendors pro rata in accordance with their respective holdings of the shares being acquired, or as otherwise directed in writing by the applicable Vendor and permitted by applicable securities laws. The Consideration Shares will be subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, or such other resale restrictions as may be required by applicable securities laws and Canadian Securities Exchange ("CSE") policies.

Upon execution of the LOI, the Company paid Privco a cash deposit of $10,000 (the "Deposit"). The Deposit is retained by Privco for its own account and is non-refundable in all circumstances, including if the LOI is terminated or the Acquisition is not completed for any reason, including failure to obtain required approvals. The Deposit is in addition to the consideration payable for the shares of Privco and will not be credited against or otherwise applied toward the Consideration Shares.

The LOI requires the definitive documentation to provide for the waiver and release, effective upon completion of the Acquisition, of the contemplated joint venture arrangements and related free-carried interest provisions under the Initial Agreement. Following completion of the Acquisition, the Vendors are expected to hold approximately 60% of the Company's issued and outstanding common shares. The Acquisition is not expected to result in the creation of a new control person of the Company.

Completion of the Acquisition is subject to the execution of the Definitive Agreement and customary closing conditions, including receipt of all required consents and the approval of the CSE. There can be no assurance that the Definitive Agreement will be executed or that the Acquisition will be completed on the terms described herein or at all.

The LOI provides for a 60-day exclusivity period during which Privco must deal exclusively with the Company in relation to the Acquisition. The Vendors are not bound by those exclusivity obligations.

Related Party Transaction

Mark Richardson, P.Geo., Vice President Exploration of the Company, is one of the Vendors and is expected to receive Consideration Shares in exchange for his common shares of Privco. His participation in the Acquisition constitutes a "related party transaction" within the meaning of Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"). The Company intends to rely on the exemptions from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements contained in sections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101, respectively, on the basis that neither the fair market value of the subject matter of the Acquisition, nor the fair market value of the consideration therefor, insofar as it involves interested parties, exceeds 25% of the Company's market capitalization, calculated in accordance with MI 61-101.

Qualified Person

Mark Richardson, P.Geo., Vice President Exploration of the Company, is a "qualified person" as defined in National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects and has reviewed and approved the technical content of this news release. Mr. Richardson is not independent of the Company.

The historical drill and surface-sampling information disclosed in this release has been compiled from publicly available Pacific Ridge exploration disclosures and Bayridge's previously published technical disclosure. The Qualified Person has reviewed these reported results against available historical and previously published information; however, the underlying historical sampling, analytical and assay data have not been independently confirmed through examination of all original laboratory certificates, resampling or reanalysis. The historical boulder-sample result has likewise not been independently confirmed by new sampling. Such independent field and laboratory verification has not been undertaken for this corporate transaction announcement, which does not report new exploration results. These limitations should be considered when interpreting the historical results; further verification would be required to support future reliance on individual historical results, as appropriate.

About Bayridge Resources Corp.

Bayridge Resources Corp. is a green energy company advancing its portfolio of Canadian uranium projects. The Company holds 51% of the Baker Lake Uranium Project, which covers 619 km² in the Kivalliq Region of Nunavut. The Company holds a 40% interest in the 1,337-ha Waterbury East project, which it operates as a joint venture with CanAlaska Uranium Ltd. (TSXV: CVV), the holder of the remaining 60% interest and project operator. Waterbury East is located 25 km northeast of the Cigar Lake Mine in the northeastern Athabasca Basin region. There, geophysical surveys have identified a 7 km long conductivity corridor where mid-2000s drilling highlighted faulted and altered basement rock with local uranium enrichment. Large sections of this corridor remain untested.

Companies partnering on project to engineer Canadian-made technology that provides operators with access to a secure, Canadian-controlled network

(TSXV: FAN) (OTCQB: FANCF) (FSE: P210) ("First Atlantic" or the "Company") is pleased to announce its attendance at the Fastmarkets Critical Minerals and Materials Briefing, taking place today, November 19, 2026, on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC.1 The Company is attending to highlight the new cerium refining technology developed at Columbia University. As reported on November 18, 2026,2 the technology extracted 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt in 20 minutes from awaruite (Ni-Fe-Co alloy) concentrate sourced from the Company's Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt Alloy Project, with approximately 90% of the nickel extracted within the first 5 minutes. The process operated at room temperature, with no smelting and no sulfuric acid pretreatment, as reported on November 18, 2026.3

First Atlantic has also launched a new website at www.fanickel.com, featuring an interactive chart of the cerium refining results, drill results and interactive maps of the Pipestone XL Project.

The briefing is being held on Capitol Hill4, and brings together federal policymakers, critical minerals producers and processors, defense and aerospace leaders, investors and industrial buyers to examine the next phase of U.S. critical minerals strategy, including domestic mining, processing and refining capacity. The program includes a fireside chat, "What's Next for Critical Minerals? U.S. Policy Priorities," with U.S. Representatives Gary Palmer and Paul Tonko, Chairman and Ranking Member respectively, of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Environment. First Atlantic Chief Executive Officer Adrian Smith and Strategic Advisor Dr. Douglas Wicks, former Program Director of the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER program and Geologic Hydrogen portfolio, are attending on behalf of the Company.

Gary Stanley, Strategic Advisor to First Atlantic and former Director of the Office of Critical Minerals and Metals at the U.S. Department of Commerce, is a panelist on "Critical Minerals and U.S. Defense Readiness: Securing Strategic Supply Chains" alongside Jeffrey Frankston, Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Industrial Base Resilience at the U.S. Department of War.5 First Atlantic welcomes the opportunity to meet with government, defense and industry representatives during the briefing.

First Atlantic is working with Columbia University, its Research Partner, to advance the new breakthrough cerium refining technology developed at Columbia University as a domestic refining option for awaruite (Ni-Fe-Co alloy), a naturally occurring magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy that is concentrated by magnetic separation and flotation without smelting.6 The Columbia University research was funded by the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER program, which was created to increase domestic production of critical minerals such as nickel and cobalt. Nickel sulfide concentrates, by contrast, must be smelted before they can be refined, and only two pyrometallurgical nickel smelters remain in operation in North America, both in Sudbury, Ontario, while the only nickel smelter in the United States, in Riddle, Oregon, closed permanently in 1998.7 Because awaruite does not need a smelter, the Columbia University research indicates strong potential for First Atlantic to develop a vertically integrated, onshore nickel and cobalt supply chain in North America: mining and concentrating awaruite at Pipestone XL in Newfoundland, then shipping a high-grade nickel-cobalt alloy concentrate directly into downstream refining to produce Class 1 nickel metal or nickel sulfate (NiSO₄), without a smelting step.

First Atlantic welcomes direct calls from shareholders and prospective investors. Rob Guzman, Investor Relations, is available at +1-844-592-6337 or by email at rob@fanickel.com to answer questions about this news release or the Company. Because call volume is high, please leave a voice message or email Rob to request a call back.

  • Capitol Hill briefing on U.S. critical minerals strategy: First Atlantic is attending the Fastmarkets Critical Minerals and Materials Briefing 2026 in Washington, DC, where Strategic Advisor Gary Stanley is a panelist on "Critical Minerals and U.S. Defense Readiness: Securing Strategic Supply Chains."
  • New cerium refining technology: Columbia University research funded by the U.S. Department of Energy’s ARPA-E MINER program extracted 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt from Pipestone XL awaruite concentrate in 20 minutes, with approximately 90% of the nickel extracted in the first 5 minutes (see Figure 2).
  • Cerium is recycled and reused in the refining loop: The cerium solution works at room temperature and atmospheric pressure, with no sulfuric acid pretreatment. Spent cerium(III) is converted back to cerium(IV) by electrochemical regeneration and reused in the leach in a closed-loop process design (see Figure 3).
  • Awaruite nickel-cobalt alloy outperformed nickel sulfide: Compared with nickel sulfide samples from Tamarack, awaruite yielded up to 66% more nickel extraction in one-third of the time, while the sulfide samples consumed up to 16 times more cerium (see Table 1).
  • High-grade magnetic alloy concentrate with no smelting required: The Company's ONSHORE MAX™ process produced a magnetic alloy concentrate averaging 67.4% nickel, grading up to 71.9% nickel and 1.76% cobalt, compared with 10% to 15% nickel in typical sulfide concentrates.
  • Vertically integrated North American supply chain: Mining and concentrating awaruite in Newfoundland, then refining the alloy concentrate in the United States with cerium refining technology, has the potential to keep nickel and cobalt in North America from mine to refined metal.
  • U.S. government engagement: First Atlantic is a member of the Defense Industrial Base Consortium (DIBC) and has applied under RPP-CM-26-01, "Domestic Processing Capabilities of Critical Minerals," with Columbia University as its Research Partner.
  • New website launched: First Atlantic has launched a new website at www.fanickel.com, featuring an interactive chart of the cerium refining results, drill results and interactive maps of the Pipestone XL Project.

Dr. Douglas Wicks, Strategic Advisor to First Atlantic and former Program Director of the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER program and Geologic Hydrogen portfolio, commented:

"The ARPA-E MINER program was created to develop commercially scalable technologies that increase domestic production of critical minerals such as nickel and cobalt. As its Program Director I funded this Columbia University research, and the results on First Atlantic's awaruite concentrate from Pipestone XL demonstrate the successful test of cerium refining: approximately 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt extracted in 20 minutes, at room temperature, without smelting or sulfuric acid. Because the cerium is regenerated with electricity and reused, the process has the potential to be cost-effective and scalable to commercial production, and to help onshore the refining of Class 1 nickel metal or battery-grade nickel in North America."
